create_engines.goggles.cam_ratio.wrong: Must turn at half crank speed
create_engines.goggles.cycle.no_air: Misfire: no fresh air in the cylinder
create_engines.goggles.fault.intake_bloc: Intake has no open air intake
create_engines.goggles.fault.no_cam: No cam lobe touching the head
create_engines.goggles.fault.not_on_thro: Not mounted on a crank throw
create_engines.goggles.head: Cylinder Head
create_engines.goggles.head.no_injector: Right-click with a Fuel Injector to install
create_engines.goggles.head.oil: Takes Engine Oil as well as fuel: it lubricates the whole engine
create_engines.goggles.lubrication.dry: Dry parts drag: pipe Engine Oil into a cylinder head
create_engines.goggles.phase: Top dead centre at crank angle %1$s°
create_engines.goggles.starter.idle: Idle: needs a redstone signal and input rotation
create_engines.goggles.state.coasting: Coasting: turning, but nothing is firing
create_engines.goggles.state.overloaded: Overloaded: load is more than its rated torque
create_engines.ponder.airflow.text_1: Every cylinder head needs an intake and an exhaust on its free faces.
create_engines.ponder.airflow.text_2: Intake Manifolds join many heads to an Air Intake. Whichever face a manifold touches becomes that head's intake.
create_engines.ponder.airflow.text_3: Exhaust Manifolds do the same for an Exhaust Outlet. Each opening comfortably serves two cylinders.
create_engines.ponder.airflow.text_4: Openings need a clear mouth. Covering the air intake starves every cylinder on it; an engine that cannot exhaust chokes on its own burned gas.
create_engines.ponder.airflow.text_5: Smoke from the outlet follows each firing. Black smoke means more fuel than air: the engine is running rich.
create_engines.ponder.camshaft.text_1: A Cam Lobe touching a cylinder head opens its valves and fires its injector as the camshaft turns.
create_engines.ponder.camshaft.text_2: In a four-stroke engine the camshaft must turn at exactly half crank speed. Gear it from the crank, for example with a small cogwheel driving a large one.
create_engines.ponder.camshaft.text_3: The Lobe Angle, set with the value panel, decides when the valves open compared with the piston. Goggles show if it is on time, early or late.
create_engines.ponder.camshaft.text_4: Two angles 180° apart both work: each picks which crank revolution the cylinder fires on. This is how firing order is set.
create_engines.ponder.camshaft.text_5: A redstone signal on the camshaft closes the fuel rack. A full-strength signal cuts the fuel and stops the engine.
create_engines.ponder.crankshaft.text_1: A crankshaft is a line of Crankshaft and Crank Throw blocks on one axis. It turns like any Create shaft.
create_engines.ponder.crankshaft.text_2: Crank Throws carry an offset crank pin. Cylinders mount on any of their four sides.
create_engines.ponder.crankshaft.text_3: Each piston reaches the top of its stroke when the crank pin points up its bore.
create_engines.ponder.crankshaft.text_4: A throw's angle can be changed with its value panel. Here the second throw is turned 180°, so its piston moves opposite the first.
create_engines.ponder.crankshaft.text_5: Cylinders on different faces of one throw share its pin. This makes a V layout: you never pick an engine type, you build it.
create_engines.ponder.crankshaft.text_6: One crankshaft is one engine. It drives the kinetic network through the shafts and gears at its ends.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_1: A Cylinder sits on a Crank Throw, its bore pointing away from the crank.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_2: Install a Connecting Rod and an Engine Piston by right-clicking. Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to take them out.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_3: A Cylinder Head closes the bore. It holds the valves and a Fuel Injector, which must be installed.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_4: The head's other faces are its connections: an intake, an exhaust, and a Cam Lobe to work the valves and injector.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_5: Fuel is piped into any face of a head. Heads that touch share their fuel, so one pipe can feed a whole bank.
create_engines.ponder.cylinder.text_6: Goggles on any engine part show whether that cylinder is firing, and if not, why.
create_engines.ponder.starter.text_1: A Starter cranks the crankshaft block it faces. It is not connected to the engine's own kinetic network.
create_engines.ponder.starter.text_2: Feed it rotation through its back from any source. It cranks the engine at the speed it is turned.
create_engines.ponder.starter.text_3: It engages while powered by redstone. Turning a dead engine over takes effort, which appears as stress on the starter's input.
create_engines.ponder.starter.text_4: Once the engine fires and runs faster than the starter, a one-way clutch lets go. Remove the signal and it carries on by itself.
create_engines.ponder.starter.text_5: A Hand Crank on the crankshaft also works for small engines. Bigger engines need stronger starters.
